name: Proxmox_VE_Topology
description: Cluster, node and guest topology for Proxmox VE: cluster to node, node to guest.
technicalNotes:
Emits two kinds of edge. Cluster to node, type "Cluster". Node to guest, type "Compute", which is the edge that matters: it lets a node's alerts explain the alerts of the guests it hosts.

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by MAC address, read from the guest config (net0 and friends). This works because LogicMonitor already keys a monitored Linux resource on its MAC addresses, so the two ERIs meet with no name matching -- a Proxmox guest called "KTV" whose resource is called "KTV - PiKaraoke" still connects. It is the same identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses. A guest with no readable MAC falls back to a synthesised key and appears on the map without resolving to a resource, exactly as the VMware module does.

Nodes cannot be matched that way. Proxmox exposes no hardware UUID and no MAC for a node anywhere in its API, so the node key is synthesised from the cluster and node names, and the companion PropertySource addERI_Proxmox_VE stamps the identical key on each node's own resource. A node whose resource has not run that PropertySource still appears on the map, but as a vertex matching nothing, so its alerts will not suppress its guests'. On the one-resource-per-cluster layout that docs/INSTALL.md recommends, only the node carrying the token runs the PropertySource; setting the token on every node makes every node match, at the duplication cost INSTALL section 4.1 describes.

Cost: one /cluster/status, one /cluster/resources per type, and one config read per guest. That last is O(guests), which DESIGN section 2 rules out for a metric module -- but this runs hourly rather than every five minutes, and the MAC is available nowhere else, since /cluster/resources carries no network detail.

This is the only module in the suite that cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector. LogicMonitor's own topology scripts do all their work through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets -- eriPreProcessor for key normalisation, isMac for validation, generateTopology for the output format -- and reimplementing those would mean inventing a format LogicMonitor does not fully document. The build emits it to dist/scripts/collector-only/ for that reason.

UNVERIFIED: neither this module nor addERI_Proxmox_VE has been imported into a portal. The export shape here was taken from a real VMware_vCenter_Cluster_Topology export, but the registryMetadata and integrationMetadata blocks a published module carries are Exchange lineage and are not fabricated here; whether an import requires them is unproven. Confirm the module imports, that a map renders, and that guest vertices resolve to the guests' own resources rather than to bare vertices.
